beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about a severity correction an LLM review step computes and writes down, that the email generator downstream never actually reads, so a corrected label keeps shipping under its old, wrong value, every single time.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: name + one-line plain-language summary, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: Our pipeline added a second opinion. An LLM reviews every high-urgency alert and can correct a wrong severity label, downgrade a false Critical to High, without rejecting the item outright. But the node that actually counts and buckets items for the alert email never learned to read that correction.
beats.new_visual_element: Two labels side by side: what the LLM corrected the severity to, versus what the email actually showed — visually flagged as a mismatch

shot.note: Real framing of the computed-but-discarded correction, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real code. Layer 2, the LLM re-score step, writes back four fields on every item it reviews: llm reviewed, llm verdict, llm corrected impact level, llm downgrade. The whole point is it can correct a label, not just reject an item. But Generate Email, the node that buckets Critical and High for the alert, only ever reads impact level, the original keyword score. The correction is computed, written, and never looked at again.
beats.new_visual_element: The real fields Layer 2 writes back, shown verbatim, next to the real two-line bucketing from Generate Email that reads only the original impact_level

shot.note: [Source: workflow.dev.json, 'Layer 2 - LLM Re-Score' and 'Generate Email' nodes] Verbatim field names and the real pre-fix bucketing lines, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: The fix adds one helper: effective impact. It prefers the LLM's correction when the item was reviewed and a correction exists, and falls back to the original label otherwise. Critical and High now filter on that, not the raw field. An item the LLM never touched behaves exactly as it did before.
beats.new_visual_element: The real diff from the Generate Email node: the old two-line bucketing struck through, the new effectiveImpact helper and its two filter lines added

shot.note: [Source: C3-VERIFICATION.md, 'The fix'] Real diff, matches the committed fix exactly.

beats.narration_text: I extracted the real, patched code from Generate Email and ran it in a live Node harness against three items covering every real case: confirmed and recategorized, confirmed with no change, and never reviewed. Before the fix: two Critical, one High. The recategorized item still counted Critical. After the fix: one Critical, two High. That same item now counts correctly. The other two are unchanged, no regression. Ran it again against the real patched file on disk, same result.
beats.new_visual_element: The real before/after table from this session's live Node.js harness run: per-item bucket, plus the critical_count/high_count totals, before and after

shot.note: [Source: verification/verify_effective_severity_output.txt] Real measured harness results from this session, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Two honest limits. First: this only changes Generate Email's bucketing. Layer 2's own review logic, the High Priority Filter's downgrade gate, and the two earlier fixes already closed in this same node are all untouched. Second, a separate defect turned up the same week in the dashboard's own stats endpoint. It re-buckets by raw urgency score with cutoffs that disagree with impact level, affecting fifty seven of four hundred eleven real rows. Not fixed this week, flagged for later.
beats.new_visual_element: 2 honest-limit cards, side by side, full weight: what this fix does and doesn't touch, and a separate open issue found but not fixed this week

shot.note: [Source: C3-VERIFICATION.md 'What's NOT touched'; RUN_LOG.md 2026-10-27 'Open issues'] Full weight, not softened.

beats.narration_text: A correction that's computed but never read isn't a correction. If a review step is allowed to change a label, every downstream consumer of that label has to actually check whether it did.
